hypothesis: B1 (found by the review layer): generate_random_case returns an all-True mask (never None) at padding_ratio<=0, so the seed always built an additive [B,1,S,S] mask -- disqualifying SDPA flash on every shape and OOMing shape #14 (~1.2 TB mask). Fix: detect no-padding once (single sync), collapse the all-True mask to None so attention uses is_causal (flash/mem-efficient).

eval.note: Final numbers, official protocol. All 12/12 shapes correct on all 3 candidates, max_abs ~1e-6 (normal fp32 non-associativity, far under the 0.002 gate). v_compile still leads by geomean (2.25x) but the lead over v_fused_qkv (2.09x) and the seed (1.96x) is narrow -- the earlier iter-5 number (2.71x/2.53x) was inflated by the noisy short-warmup protocol and should not be reported. Shape #14 still not attempted (B5).

hypothesis: Confirm B5 (shape #14 infeasible in fp32 on A100-80) with real measured OOM/timeout evidence instead of estimated math, on all 3 candidates.

eval.note: best.py and v_fused_qkv.py both OOM during optimized-model warmup (73.85GB in use, tried to alloc 12.21GB more, 79.25GB total) -- confirms B5s ~85GB estimate, and shows the OOM is from plain [B,S,D] activation size, not attention algorithm (flash/mem-efficient SDPA already in use). v_compile.py never reached the OOM point -- Slurm killed it at the 15min time limit still inside max-autotune (each large matmul took ~100s x ~15 candidate kernels to autotune). Conclusion: infeasible in fp32 on any GPU we have, for two independent reasons (memory ceiling, and separately compile-time cost). Not pursuing fp16/H100/chunking -- out of scope per TODO.md B5 and rubric SS3.3.

eval.note: Forced flash/mem_efficient/math per shape via torch.nn.attention.sdpa_kernel on all 14 official shapes. Flash eligible on ZERO shapes (fp16/bf16-only, confirmed independent of head_dim -- even head_dim=8/32 shapes that B7 predicted flash-eligible are not, at fp32). mem_efficient fires on all 14. Settles PROGRAM.md:61 ("biggest single win [is flash]") as false as measured -- mem-efficient SDPA is what has actually been running in every benchmark in this repo so far. Does not change any existing speedup number (mem-efficient was already firing), only what to call it in the report. Raw data: docs/sdpa_backend_probe.json.

eval.note: Beats every single candidate: v_router 2.27x/2.47x vs v_compile 2.18x/2.25x, v_fused_qkv 2.16x/2.09x, best 2.07x/1.96x (all iter-6 numbers). First version of this file dynamically imported sibling candidate files by __file__-relative path and broke on the cluster (FileNotFoundError -- runner.py scp-ships each candidate alone into a per-job temp dir). Fixed by making it a self-contained snapshot like v_compile.py/v_fused_qkv.py, inlining all three implementations. Verified the fix by reproducing the exact isolated-directory scenario locally before re-running on A100. Per-shape numbers vs the route table built from iter 6 differ by 1-5%% (run-to-run noise) but every routing choice still held up -- light reproducibility check.
